newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-TROUSSIER PROMISES NIGERIA PLACE AT WORLD CUP FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TROUSSIER PROMISES NIGERIA PLACE AT WORLD CUP FINALS.

text.p: Frenchman Philippe Troussier, who was appointed by Olympic champions Nigeria as their new manager last month, pledged on Friday to take the nation to the 1998 World Cup finals in France.

Nigeria are currently second behind Guinea in their World Cup qualifying group. The Nigerians, who came within a minute of beating Italy and gaining a quarter-final place in the 1994 World Cup, face Guinea in Lagos on April 5.
Troussier, at a formal signing ceremony of his contract in Lagos, told reporters that Nigeria could rely on his knowledge of African soccer and coaching acumen to get them to the finals.
"I promise you I will take Nigeria to next year's World Cup and it's an objective which must be achieved," he said.
Abdulmumini Aminu, chairman of the Nigeria Football Association, said Troussier's contract was in two phases.

"The first phase is for six months and he will earn a salary of $10,000 monthly. If we qualify for the World Cup, then we will re-negotiate with him to draft the contract till after the World Cup," Aminu said. He did not comment on what would happen if Nigeria failed to qualify for the World Cup finals.

Troussier, 42, is the 16th foreign national and the first Frenchman to coach Nigeria. He replaces Dutchman Jo Bonfrere who quit the job in October after alleging poor treatment and interference in his duties.
The Nigerian soccer authorities in January sacked local coach Amodu Shaibu who had taken over the team on a temporary basis.
Aminu said: "Troussier's morale should not be dampened by the friction we had with these coaches. We will provide the support and right atmosphere for him to work and succeed."

Troussier, nicknamed "White Wizard", was trainer of Moroccan first division team FUS Rabat. He has also trained first division teams ASEC Mimosas and Kaiser Chiefs in Ivory Coast and South Africa, respectively.
He was Ivory Coast coach in 1993 but lost the job after that country failed to qualify for the 1994 World Cup from the group from which Nigeria qualified.
"All that is history. Now I will make more history as the first Frenchman to take Nigeria to its second World Cup finals," he said good-humouredly.
